topics.title: A poem about the work people do

learn.hook: The baker, the painter, the farmer, the postman... Every day we see people doing different work. Which would you like to do?
points: Poems about work show us the many jobs people do around us.
A vocation is the work a person chooses or feels they are meant to do.
Children often dream about what they will be when they grow up.
Each pair of lines in this poem rhymes: bread-shed, wheat-street, tall-all.
Every kind of honest work is useful and deserves respect.

example.q: Read the poem: I watch the baker knead the bread, / I watch the painter paint the shed. / The farmer sows the seeds of wheat, / The postman cycles down our street. / I wonder, when I'm grown and tall, / Which one I'll be, or maybe all! What does the child in the poem wonder about?
steps: Look at the last two lines.
'I wonder, when I'm grown and tall, / Which one I'll be, or maybe all!'
So the child wonders which work they will do when they grow up.
example.answer: Which of these jobs they will do when they grow up, or maybe all of them!

learn.reallife: Think of the people who help your family every day: the vegetable seller, the bus driver, the doctor, the teacher. Each has a vocation.

games.title: About the poem
items: In the poem, the painter paints the shed.
'I watch the painter paint the shed.'
The farmer sows seeds of rice.
The poem says the farmer sows the seeds of wheat.
The postman cycles down the street.
The child has already chosen one job.
The child still wonders 'Which one I'll be, or maybe all!'

quiz.q: Read: 'I watch the baker knead the bread.' What is the baker doing?
quiz.explain: The line says the baker kneads the bread.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the workers in the poem

quiz.q: Read: 'The postman cycles down our street.' Who cycles down the street?
quiz.explain: The line names the postman.
quiz.mistake: Picks a worker from another line

quiz.q: Read: 'The farmer sows the seeds of wheat.' What does the farmer sow?
quiz.explain: The farmer sows wheat seeds.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the line carefully

quiz.q: Read: 'The farmer sows the seeds of wheat, / The postman cycles down our street.' Which word rhymes with 'wheat'?
quiz.explain: 'Wheat' and 'street' end with the same sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from the lines that does not rhyme

quiz.q: Read: 'I wonder, when I'm grown and tall, / Which one I'll be, or maybe all!' What is the child wondering?
options: Which work they will do when they grow up
quiz.explain: The child wonders which of these jobs they will choose one day.
quiz.mistake: Takes the words 'grown and tall' too literally

quiz.q: Read: 'I watch the baker knead the bread.' What does 'knead' mean?
options: To press and fold dough with the hands
quiz.explain: Knead means to press and fold dough. It sounds like 'need', but the meaning is different.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'knead' with its sound-alike 'need'

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'tall' in the poem?
quiz.explain: 'Tall' and 'all' end with the same '-all' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word without checking the ending sound

quiz.q: What is the poem mainly about?
options: The work people do and a child's dreams
quiz.explain: It describes workers and ends with the child wondering about the future.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the whole poem

teach.ask: Gappu peeks out: 'What work do people do in the poem? What is a vocation?'
teach.praise: When I grow up, I want to be a teacher just like you!
teach.nudge: Which workers are in the poem? And what is a vocation?

learn.hook: A person who teaches is a teacher. A person who sails is a sailor. Can you guess what a person who paints is called?
points: An occupation is the work a person does to earn a living.
Many worker words are made by adding -er: teach-teacher, farm-farmer, bake-baker.
Some end in -ist or -ian: art-artist, violin-violinist, music-musician, science-scientist.
Some worker words are special: a cobbler mends shoes, a carpenter works with wood.

example.q: What do we call a person who paints, and how is the word made?
steps: Start with the action word: paint.

learn.reallife: On Career Day at school, children dress up as doctors, pilots, scientists and chefs. Each worker word tells what the person does!

quiz.q: What is a person who teaches called?
quiz.explain: teach + er = teacher.
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong ending

quiz.q: What is a person who sails a ship called?
quiz.explain: Sail takes the ending -or: sailor.
quiz.mistake: Adds -er to every word

quiz.q: What is a person who plays music called?
quiz.explain: Music takes the ending -ian: musician.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the -ian ending

quiz.q: What do we call a person who studies science?
quiz.explain: Science becomes scientist.
quiz.mistake: Adds an ending without changing the word

quiz.q: Who fixes the wires, switches and fans in a house?
quiz.explain: An electrician works with electric wiring.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the work of different people

quiz.q: What is a person who acts in plays or films called?
quiz.explain: act + or = actor.
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong ending

quiz.q: Who mends shoes?
quiz.explain: A cobbler mends and makes shoes. A carpenter works with wood.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up special worker words

quiz.q: What does 'occupation' mean?
options: The work a person does to earn a living
quiz.explain: Your occupation is your job or work.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word 'occupation'

teach.ask: Gappu wears a tiny cap: 'I sing, so am I a sing-ist? How do we make words for workers?'
teach.praise: So I am a singer! Thank you for the lesson, teacher!
teach.nudge: Which endings make worker words? Can you give me an example?

learn.hook: 'When I grow up, I will...' Finish that sentence! Today we learn how to talk about the future.
points: We use 'will' + the base verb to talk about the future: I will become a doctor.
'will not' can be shortened to 'won't': I won't give up.
'going to' shows a plan: I am going to learn the tabla.
We can share dreams with 'want to' or 'would like to': I want to be a pilot.
Every dream needs effort today: practise, read and keep asking questions.

example.q: Change to the future: 'Asha paints a picture.'
steps: To talk about the future, use 'will'.
After 'will', use the base verb: paint, not paints.

learn.reallife: On New Year's Day, many people say what they will do in the coming year. These are plans for the future!

items.text: She will ___ a song at the function.
From now on, I ___ forget my homework!
I am ___ to learn swimming this summer.

games.title: Make a sentence
games.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence

quiz.q: What is the future form of 'I paint'?
quiz.explain: Future: will + base verb. So 'I will paint'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s or uses the past form after 'will'

quiz.q: Choose: 'When I grow up, I ___ a pilot.'
quiz.explain: 'When I grow up' points to the future, so we use 'will become'.
quiz.mistake: Uses a past or -s form for the future

quiz.q: Which sentence is about the future?
options: Riya will visit the museum tomorrow.
Riya visits the museum on Sundays.
Riya is visiting the museum now.
quiz.explain: 'Will visit' and 'tomorrow' show the future.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up tenses

quiz.q: What is the short form of 'will not'?
quiz.explain: 'Will not' becomes 'won't', with the apostrophe between n and t.
quiz.mistake: Puts the apostrophe in the wrong place or makes up a form

quiz.q: Choose: 'Next week, we ___ trees in the school garden.'
quiz.explain: 'Next week' is in the future, so we use 'will plant'.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the time words 'next week'

quiz.q: Which future-tense sentence is correct?
options: She will dances at the function.
She will dance at the function.
She will danced at the function.
She will dancing at the function.
quiz.explain: After 'will' we always use the base verb: dance.
quiz.mistake: Changes the verb after 'will'

quiz.q: Read: 'I am going to learn the tabla.' What does this sentence show?
quiz.explain: 'Going to' shows a plan for the future.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'going' means moving somewhere

quiz.q: Which sentence tells about a dream for the future?
options: I want to be a scientist when I grow up.
I am sitting in class now.
quiz.explain: It tells what the speaker wishes to become in the future.
quiz.mistake: Picks a sentence about the past or present

teach.ask: Gappu dreams: 'One day I ___ fly to the moon! How do I talk about the future?'
teach.praise: One day I will fly high, and I will remember your lesson!
teach.nudge: Which word helps us talk about the future? What comes after it?
